My complaints with the game are mostly mechanical, though the writing does turn me off of many of the characters.

The gunplay is very bad, mostly due to the enemy AI. In Cyberpunk, enemies will either take cover in one spot and never move, or they will charge you. That's it. By contrast, enemies in F.E.A.R., a 15-year-old game, will call out your position to each other, flank you and push together, and lay down suppressing fire for each other when they advance. Same thing with the AI enemies in A.R.M.A. games or Escape from Tarkov.

As a general rule of thumb for single player FPS games, if you can just repeatedly pop out of cover from a single location without ever having to reposition or flank your enemies with little to no risk of dying, I consider the gameplay to be bad. Couple this with the extremely poorly balanced weapons--shooting a human enemy point blank in the soft part of their head with a revolver does almost no damage while slapping them in their robotic exoskeleton with a baseball bat does literally 10x the damage--it's just not fun.

The melee combat is also pretty bad. Weapons have no weight to them. It just feels like slapping your enemies with a wet noodle until they die. With games like Chivalry: Medieval Warfare and to a greater extent Mordhau setting the bar for First Person Melee combat with teams of less than 10 developers, I am surprised that AAA with thousands of employees can't make a decent melee system. Blocking seems to be completely arbitrary whether it works or not. I have blocked an enemy melee with full stamina and taken no damage, I have blocked the exact same enemy with full stamina and gotten hit, and there doesn't seem to be a meaningful difference or reason why.

The driving is awful. Every single vehicle way oversteers on Keyboard. It's like trying to drive on ice with buttered up wheels. Not to mention that parking anywhere causes a crowd of 30 civilians to shout "OH MY GOD HE'S ON A RAMPAGE" and run away or cower in fear.

Speaking of civilians, cowering or running away in fear is all that they can do. The only NPCs that fight back are cops and designated bad guys. How come GTA3, a 20 year old game, did this better than Cyberpunk?
